tasks.prompt: After a power outage, a lift station restarts but one pump runs without moving any sewage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station after a utility outage and restart. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Pump 1 runs with normal amps but wet well level does not fall while it runs.
Pump 2 lowers the wet well normally when it runs.
Pump 1 discharge pressure gauge reads near zero while it runs.
The outage caused a brief reverse flow in the force main before restart.
Opening Pump 1 volute bleed releases a large volume of trapped air, after which it pumps normally.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pump 1 check valve is stuck fully closed
Pump 1 was air bound after the outage and reverse flow, and venting restored it
The wet well level sensor froze during the outage
Pump 1 impeller sheared off during the outage

inference.explanation: A sheared impeller would not recover with venting, and the level sensor is proven by Pump 2 behaviour. Air release followed by normal pumping confirms air binding as the cause.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Level sensor replacement
Pump 1 impeller replacement
An air release check at the pump and force main high point after every outage restart, added to the restart checklist

nextClue.explanation: Adding the venting check to restart steps prevents a repeat of the confirmed air binding.

clueText.nc-a: The pump recovered fully after venting, so the impeller is intact.
clueText.nc-b: The sensor tracked Pump 2 drawdown correctly, so it is not frozen.
clueText.nc-c: At the next outage restart, venting clears air and both pumps draw down normally.

tasks.prompt: A supervisor reviews a station that had four overflow events in a year, all during storms, with pumps in good condition.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station overflow review under Ontario Regulation 129/04 duties. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: All four overflows occurred when catchment inflow exceeded the firm pumping capacity, with one pump out of service as the design basis.
Both pumps are maintained and meet rated capacity on tests.
Wet weather inflow records show catchment peaks growing each year as inflow sources were added.
No generator or control failures occurred during the four events.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The station is capacity limited against growing wet weather inflow, not suffering equipment failure
The pumps are failing during storms despite passing tests
The operator on duty caused all four overflows
The overflows were reporting errors and did not occur

inference.explanation: Pumps test at rating, controls and power did not fail, and inflow above firm capacity explains each event. Growing peaks from added inflow sources explain why events cluster in recent storms.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A pump overhaul program as the sole response
A capacity and inflow study, firm capacity against current wet weather peaks, as the basis for an upgrade or inflow reduction plan
Discipline review for the operators on duty

nextClue.explanation: The study sizes the gap between firm capacity and current peaks, which is the decision the upgrade depends on.

clueText.nc-a: No operator error is recorded in any event log, and pumps performed to rating.
clueText.nc-b: The study shows peaks now exceed firm capacity by 25 percent in a one in five year storm.
clueText.nc-c: Pumps already meet rating, so overhaul does not close a capacity gap.

tasks.prompt: Wet well levels at a station creep upward over months even though daily inflow volumes are unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station with level and run records over six months. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Average wet well operating level has risen steadily over six months at the same daily inflow.
Pump run times per cycle have lengthened while cycles per day are unchanged.
Drawdown tests show both pumps now deliver 20 percent below their rating from a year ago.
Force main pressure at the station has risen over the same period at the same flows.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Rising force main resistance, from buildup or a partly closed valve, is reducing delivered pump capacity
Residents are discharging in longer cycles
The level floats have drifted upward
Inflow has secretly increased over the six months

inference.explanation: Daily inflow is stated unchanged, longer runs at lower delivered rate match the drawdown loss, and rising force main pressure at the same flow points downstream of the pumps. Float drift would not change drawdown test results.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Float recalibration as the sole action
An inflow records audit only
Force main pressure profiling and valve position checks along the main

nextClue.explanation: Profiling pressure and checking valves locates the added resistance the pressure trend indicates.

clueText.nc-a: Drawdown tests measure real delivered flow, so float drift cannot explain them.
clueText.nc-b: Inflow volumes are unchanged in the records the audit would recheck.
clueText.nc-c: Profiling finds a partly closed valve and heavy buildup in one reach, matching the pressure rise.

tasks.prompt: A station alternator fails to switch duty, so the same pump runs for weeks and wears early.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario duplex station with an alternator fault review. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Run hour meters show Pump 1 logged 95 percent of station hours over two months.
Pump 2 starts and runs normally whenever it is selected manually.
The alternator relay is found with a burnt contact and does not change state.
Pump 1 seal failed early, consistent with continuous duty beyond its planned share.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pump 2 is faulty and the alternator correctly avoids it
Operators manually selected Pump 1 for two months
The run hour meters are miswired and swap the readings
The failed alternator relay kept Pump 1 on duty and caused its early seal wear

inference.explanation: Pump 2 runs normally on manual selection, so avoidance is not justified, and a burnt alternator contact is a direct mechanism. Meter miswiring would not produce a burnt relay or a worn seal on the logged pump.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Alternator function test added to monthly station checks, with run hour balance reviewed
Pump 2 overhaul
Run hour meter rewiring

nextClue.explanation: Testing alternation monthly catches a stuck relay before one pump absorbs all the duty again.

clueText.nc-a: Monthly tests after relay replacement show run hours balancing within 10 percent.
clueText.nc-b: Pump 2 already runs normally, so overhaul is not indicated.
clueText.nc-c: Meters matched manual run logs, so the readings were real.

tasks.prompt: A lift station surcharges its upstream sewer during storms even though a third pump was added last year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station upgraded from two pumps to three. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: With all three pumps running, station outflow is only slightly higher than with two pumps.
Force main velocity and pressure rise sharply when the third pump starts.
The force main is the original size, unchanged during the pump upgrade.
Wet well drawdown with one pump matches that pump rating exactly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Controls never actually start the third pump
The wet well is too small for three pumps
The third pump is defective and contributes nothing
The original force main is the bottleneck, so added pumps cannot raise station outflow much

inference.explanation: One pump delivers its rating, controls do start the third pump, and outflow barely rises while force main pressure climbs, which is the signature of a downstream bottleneck. A defective third pump would not raise main pressure when it starts.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A force main capacity assessment against the three pump station curve before any further pump work
Third pump replacement
Wet well enlargement design

nextClue.explanation: Assessing the force main against the combined pump curve sizes the real bottleneck.

clueText.nc-a: The assessment shows the main reaches its practical limit at about two pump flow, matching station tests.
clueText.nc-b: The third pump raises main pressure when it runs, so it is pumping, not defective.
clueText.nc-c: Drawdown behaviour is normal, so wet well size is not limiting outflow.

tasks.prompt: Frequent short cycling damages a pump motor, and the Class 3 operator must find why cycles shortened.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station with a motor failure after short cycling. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Starts per hour rose from 4 to 18 over one month before the motor failed.
The lead float was found hung up on a grease mat, narrowing the on and off level gap.
Inflow to the station did not change over that month.
After the wet well was cleaned and the float freed, starts returned to 4 per hour.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Inflow tripled and forced the extra starts
A grease fouled float narrowed the operating range and caused the short cycling that overheated the motor
The pump lost prime repeatedly on its own
The motor was defective from manufacture

inference.explanation: Inflow was unchanged, the fouled float is a direct mechanism for a narrow range, and cleaning restored normal starts. A manufacturing defect does not explain why starts rose only when the float fouled and fell when it was freed.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Motor warranty claim as the sole action
Wet well grease cleaning frequency review, with float movement checked at each visit
A catchment inflow investigation

nextClue.explanation: Checking float movement at each visit catches fouling before cycling shortens again.

clueText.nc-a: The motor ran for years before the cycling change, so a birth defect does not fit the timing.
clueText.nc-b: At the new cleaning frequency, floats stay free and starts remain near 4 per hour.
clueText.nc-c: Inflow records were flat through the cycling change, so inflow is ruled out.

tasks.prompt: A station backup power test succeeds monthly, yet the station overflowed during a real four hour outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station with a standby generator and an outage overflow. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Monthly generator tests run the generator for 20 minutes with no load transfer to the pumps.
During the real outage the generator started but its fuel ran out after 90 minutes.
The fuel tank gauge read full before the outage but a sight glass check after showed the gauge was stuck.
Wet well storage above the alarm level holds about 60 minutes of average inflow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Untested fuel supply and no load testing hid that the generator could not carry the station for a long outage
The generator engine is too small for the pumps
Operators refused to start the generator
The outage overflow was caused by storm inflow, not power loss

inference.explanation: The generator did start and run, so refusal and sizing at start are not the story, and no storm is stated. A stuck gauge hiding low fuel plus tests that never transferred load explain why monthly tests passed while a real outage failed.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A storm inflow study
Generator engine replacement
Full load generator testing with fuel verified by sight glass and a runtime calculation against outage storage

nextClue.explanation: Load testing with verified fuel proves the station can ride out an outage longer than its storage time.

clueText.nc-a: The engine carried load for 90 minutes, so it is sized for the pumps.
clueText.nc-b: No storm occurred during the outage in the event record.
clueText.nc-c: The first load test runs both pumps and the runtime calc shows fuel for 10 hours after refilling.

tasks.prompt: Two identical stations show very different pump seal failure rates, and a supervisor looks for the system cause.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario twin lift stations with the same pumps and age. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Station J seals last about four years, Station K seals fail about every eight months.
Station K wet well holds sewage much longer at low level, and its sewage arrives through a long force main from another station.
Hydrogen sulfide readings at Station K wet well are high, at Station J they are low.
Seal faces from Station K show chemical attack consistent with sulfide exposure.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Station K operators install seals incorrectly every time
Station K received a bad batch of seals
Septic, sulfide rich sewage held at Station K is attacking its pump seals
Station J seals last because its pumps run less often

inference.explanation: Long holding plus a long upstream force main make K sewage septic, sulfide readings are high there only, and the seal damage pattern matches chemical attack. Repeated bad batches or repeated install errors do not explain the sulfide readings or the damage pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Operator retraining as the sole action
A seal supplier change as the sole action
Sulfide and detention review at Station K, including upstream force main detention time

nextClue.explanation: Reviewing sulfide and detention addresses the environment the seal faces show is attacking them.

clueText.nc-a: Seals from the same supplier last four years at Station J.
clueText.nc-b: Install crews rotate between both stations, so crew error does not separate them.
clueText.nc-c: The review confirms long detention and high sulfide, and a chemical feed trial lowers both sulfide and seal attack signs.

tasks.prompt: A force main air valve at a high point sprays sewage during pump starts, then seals again.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main high point air valve investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Spraying occurs only in the first minute after a pump start, then the valve seals.
Between starts the valve weeps a small amount of air at the high point.
The valve float and seat show heavy rag and grease fouling on inspection.
Force main pressure at the high point is normal once the pump run is established.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Air is entering the main from the wet well continuously
A fouled air valve float cannot seat promptly at pump start, spraying until pressure seats it
The valve body is cracked and leaks under pressure
The force main is over pressurized at all times

inference.explanation: Pressure is normal in steady running, a cracked body would leak throughout the run, and the fouling found on the float and seat explains a slow seat at start that pressure then completes. The start only timing fits the fouled float.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Air valve cleaning and a start up observation at the high point to confirm prompt seating
Force main pressure relief installation
Valve body replacement as the first step

nextClue.explanation: Cleaning and watching a start confirms the float seats promptly once fouling is removed.

clueText.nc-a: After cleaning, three observed starts show no spray and the valve seats within seconds.
clueText.nc-b: Steady pressure was already normal, so relief is not indicated.
clueText.nc-c: The body was intact on inspection, fouling was the finding.

tasks.prompt: A force main delivers falling flow over a year while pump condition at the station tests as new.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main with a high point and no intermediate access. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Station drawdown into a test tank shows pumps deliver full rating.
Delivered flow at the discharge manhole has fallen 25 percent over a year at the same pump combination.
Pressure at the station has risen steadily at the same delivered flow.
The air valve at the single high point is found seized shut with its isolation valve closed.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The discharge manhole meter has drifted low
The force main has developed a major leak
A seized air valve lets air accumulate at the high point, shrinking the flow area and raising resistance
The pumps are worn despite the test tank result

inference.explanation: Pumps prove full rating into a test tank, and rising pressure fits added resistance, not a leak, which would lower pressure. A seized valve at the only high point supplies the air accumulation mechanism.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Pump overhaul
A leak survey along the main
Air valve repair and a delivered flow retest at the discharge manhole

nextClue.explanation: Retesting delivered flow after valve repair confirms whether resistance falls back.

clueText.nc-a: Test tank results already prove pump condition.
clueText.nc-b: A leak would lower, not raise, station pressure at the same flow.
clueText.nc-c: After repair, delivered flow returns to within 3 percent of the original value at normal pressure.

tasks.prompt: Repeated force main breaks occur at one bend downstream of a lift station, always shortly after a pump stops.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main with three breaks at the same bend in two years. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: All three breaks happened within minutes after a pump stop, never during steady running.
Steady running pressure at the bend is well below the pipe pressure rating.
Pressure logging at the station shows a sharp spike travelling from the station at each pump stop.
The station has no surge vessel and its check valves slam shut at pump stop.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Construction traffic above the bend crushes it at random times
Pressure surge at pump stop, water hammer, is overstressing the bend despite normal steady pressure
The bend pipe is corroded through from the outside
Steady operating pressure is slowly fatiguing the bend

inference.explanation: Breaks timed to pump stops, a measured travelling spike, and slamming checks with no surge protection fit water hammer. Steady pressure is well below rating, and random traffic would not time breaks to pump stops three times.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A soil corrosion survey as the sole action
Bend replacement with the same design and no surge work
Transient pressure logging at the bend during controlled pump stops, before choosing surge control

nextClue.explanation: Logging the transient at the bend sizes the surge that surge control must absorb.

clueText.nc-a: Replacing like for like leaves the spike that broke three pipes in place.
clueText.nc-b: Soil corrosion does not time failures to pump stops.
clueText.nc-c: Logging shows stop spikes well above steady pressure at the bend, confirming the design target.

tasks.prompt: An odour complaint cluster maps to one manhole, but the sewer upstream and downstream smells normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario odour investigation in a residential area. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Complaints centre on one manhole at a low point where a force main discharges into the gravity sewer.
Sewage in the force main is held for many hours between pump cycles at low flow.
Hydrogen sulfide at the discharge manhole is high, and falls to low levels within two reaches downstream.
The gravity sewer upstream of the discharge is a separate branch with low sulfide.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A dead animal in the manhole is causing the odour
A nearby restaurant grease trap is the odour source
Septic force main discharge releases sulfide at the manhole, causing the local odour cluster
The whole gravity system is septic and venting at this manhole

inference.explanation: Sulfide is high exactly at the discharge and low elsewhere, the force main holds sewage for hours which makes it septic, and the upstream branch is low. A system wide cause would not fall off within two reaches.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Manhole cleaning as the sole action
A restaurant grease trap inspection program
Sulfide logging at the discharge manhole across pump cycles to confirm release timing

nextClue.explanation: Logging across pump cycles ties sulfide peaks to discharges, confirming the release mechanism.

clueText.nc-a: Cleaning does not stop septic discharge arriving with every pump cycle.
clueText.nc-b: No grease odour pattern or trap finding is stated, and sulfide tracks the discharge.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows sulfide spiking with each force main discharge and decaying between cycles.

tasks.prompt: Crown corrosion is severe in one sewer reach while the reach below it, carrying the same sewage, is sound.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario corrosion investigation on a trunk sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The corroded reach is flat, slow, and runs half full with a wide sewage surface.
The sound reach below is steeper, faster, and runs deeper with a smaller surface ratio.
A long force main discharges septic sewage at the top of the corroded reach.
Crown samples in the corroded reach show acid attack, and headspace sulfide is high there.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sound reach was lined in secret during construction
The corroded reach pipe is a weaker material batch
Road salt runoff enters the corroded reach and attacks the crown
Septic discharge plus slow flat flow gives sulfide time and surface to form crown acid in that reach only

inference.explanation: The same sewage becomes damaging where septic input, long residence, and high headspace sulfide combine, and acid attack is confirmed on the crown. Material batch does not explain why damage starts exactly below the septic discharge.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Full length lining of both reaches
A road salt runoff study
Headspace sulfide and crown condition mapping along both reaches to define the protection limits

nextClue.explanation: Mapping sulfide and condition defines where protection is needed instead of lining sound pipe.

clueText.nc-a: The sound reach needs no lining, so full length work wastes capital.
clueText.nc-b: Crown acid attack with high sulfide is a sewer gas process, not a road salt pattern.
clueText.nc-c: Mapping shows sulfide and attack fading where the steeper reach scours and dilutes the flow.

tasks.prompt: A chemical feed for odour control is dosed at a lift station, but odours persist at the discharge manhole 2 km away.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main odour control review with dosing records. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Chemical dose is set from average daily flow at the lift station.
Force main detention varies from 2 hours at peak flow to 14 hours overnight.
Sulfide at the discharge is low on day shifts and high after overnight low flow periods.
Raising the dose only during a daytime trial did not change the overnight sulfide peaks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Overnight long detention generates more sulfide than the average based dose can control
Daytime operators are skipping the chemical feed
The discharge manhole has a separate local odour source
The chemical product is expired and inactive

inference.explanation: Sulfide tracks detention, not shift behaviour, and a daytime dose increase did not touch overnight peaks, which rules out a simple product or skipping story. Long overnight detention is the variable that matches the peaks.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Doubling the fixed dose at all hours
Flow paced and detention aware dosing trial, with sulfide logged at the discharge for two weeks
A local manhole odour survey only

nextClue.explanation: A detention aware trial tests whether matching dose to generation removes the overnight peaks.

clueText.nc-a: Doubling at all hours wastes chemical in the day, when sulfide is already low.
clueText.nc-b: The trial cuts overnight discharge sulfide sharply at a similar total chemical use.
clueText.nc-c: Sulfide timing already ties the odour to arriving force main flow, not a local source.

tasks.prompt: A FOG program reports success because inspections rose, but blockages in the target district did not fall.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario fats oils and grease program audit, Class 3 supervisory review. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Inspections completed rose 80 percent in the program year.
Grease blockages in the target district were unchanged from the year before.
Most inspections were at low risk premises, while high risk premises show overdue interceptor service records.
CCTV in the worst reach still shows fresh grease below the high risk premises.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The program measured activity, not outcomes, and missed the high risk premises that drive blockages
Blockages are caused by roots, so grease inspections cannot help
More inspections of any kind will fix the district next year
The blockage records must be wrong because inspections rose

inference.explanation: Fresh grease below overdue high risk premises ties blockages to the sites the program under visited. Activity counts rising while outcomes stay flat shows the measure, not the records, is the problem.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Doubling inspections at low risk premises
Closing the program as successful on inspection counts
Risk based re-ranking of premises with interceptor service verification at the high risk sites

nextClue.explanation: Verifying service at high risk sites tests whether enforcement there moves blockages.

clueText.nc-a: Low risk sites were already inspected heavily with no blockage change.
clueText.nc-b: Closing on counts would certify a program whose target outcome never moved.
clueText.nc-c: After service is verified at high risk sites, grease on CCTV in the worst reach falls within two quarters.

tasks.prompt: A downtown FOG blockage recurs below a food court even though every tenant has an interceptor on paper.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario food court grease investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: All food court tenants list an interceptor in their lease records.
Inspection finds one shared interceptor for the whole court, undersized for the combined load and overdue for service.
Grease in the sewer is worst after weekend peak trading.
A tenant that fries continuously discharges through a floor drain that bypasses the shared interceptor.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: An undersized shared interceptor plus a bypassing drain let food court grease reach the sewer
Residents above the food court cause the blockages
Each tenant secretly removed their own interceptor
The sewer grade alone causes the grease buildup

inference.explanation: Lease records describe paper compliance, while inspection finds the real shared undersized unit, overdue service, and a direct bypass. Peak trading timing matches food court load, not residents above.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Interceptor sizing and service verification for the food court, plus sealing the bypass drain route
Sewer grade survey as the sole action
A resident education campaign in the tower above

nextClue.explanation: Verifying size, service, and the bypass closes the paths inspection actually found.

clueText.nc-a: After service and bypass correction, weekend grease in the reach falls sharply.
clueText.nc-b: No resident source is observed, and timing follows food court trading.
clueText.nc-c: Grade does not explain a bypass drain found on inspection.

tasks.prompt: A bypass at a treatment headworks is reported as storm caused, and a supervisor must verify the cause before signing the report.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario bypass report review under Ontario Regulation 129/04 reporting duties. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The bypass occurred during a moderate rain that the plant has handled many times without bypassing.
One of two headworks screens was out of service for repair during the event.
Screenings and grit records show the working screen blinded with wipes during the event peak.
Plant inflow never exceeded the rated capacity with both screens in service.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The rain was an extreme event beyond plant design
Operators bypassed early to avoid working the peak
The bypass report is a paperwork error and no bypass occurred
Loss of screening capacity plus wipe blinding, not the moderate rain alone, caused the bypass

inference.explanation: The rain was within handled experience and inflow was within two screen capacity, while one screen was down and the other blinded. That capacity loss, not weather extremity or operator choice, explains the event.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A rainfall record correction
Signing the report as storm caused with no review
A screen redundancy and wipe load review, with bypass cause coding checked against maintenance logs

nextClue.explanation: Reviewing redundancy against maintenance logs aligns the report with the verified cause.

clueText.nc-a: Signing without review would record a cause the logs contradict.
clueText.nc-b: Rainfall records agree the event was moderate, so no correction is due.
clueText.nc-c: The review confirms the plant bypasses only when a screen is out during wipe peaks.

tasks.prompt: A sanitary sewer overflow repeats at the same manhole in dry weather, and two crews disagree on the cause.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario dry weather overflow investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The overflow manhole is just downstream of a reach with a known flat grade.
CCTV in that reach shows a debris dam of wipes and grit holding back flow.
Upstream flow is normal residential flow with no rain for a week.
Jetting the reach clears the dam and the overflow does not recur for months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Groundwater infiltration surcharged the manhole
The manhole cover was sealed and pressure built up
A downstream trunk blockage backed flow up to this manhole
A debris dam in the flat reach caused the dry weather overflow

inference.explanation: A week without rain rules out storm inflow, a visible dam sits exactly upstream, and removing it ends the problem for months. A downstream trunk blockage would show surcharge in lower manholes, which is not observed.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A trunk sewer CCTV survey first
A cleaning frequency review for the flat reach, with CCTV verification after cleaning
A groundwater study for the area

nextClue.explanation: Setting cleaning frequency from the verified dam location prevents the repeat the pattern predicts.

clueText.nc-a: The trunk below was checked during the event and flowed freely.
clueText.nc-b: On the new frequency the reach stays clear and no dry overflow recurs in a year.
clueText.nc-c: Dry weather for a week and a visible dam leave groundwater with nothing to explain.

tasks.prompt: An overflow during a storm is blamed on a lift station, but records show the station never reached its alarm level.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario storm overflow review with station and sewer records. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The overflow manhole is on a gravity branch that does not drain to the lift station in question.
Station logs show wet well levels stayed below the high level alarm through the storm.
The gravity branch has a history of root blockages at two joints.
CCTV after the storm finds a fresh root and wipe dam in that branch above the overflow manhole.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lift station failed silently with no alarm record
The storm alone surcharged a clear branch
Station logs were altered after the event
A root and wipe dam in the gravity branch caused the overflow, not the lift station

inference.explanation: The branch does not even drain to the station, station levels never alarmed, and a dam is found exactly above the overflow. A clear branch surcharge claim is contradicted by the dam found on camera.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A lift station failure investigation
A station log audit as the sole action
Root treatment and a wipe dam cleaning schedule for the gravity branch

nextClue.explanation: Treating the branch roots addresses the dam location the camera confirmed.

clueText.nc-a: The station cannot fail a branch that does not drain to it.
clueText.nc-b: Logs match the separate level recorder, so alteration is not supported.
clueText.nc-c: After root treatment the branch passes the next matched storm with no overflow.

tasks.prompt: A CIPP lining project claims success, but downstream flows show the problem moved rather than ended.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lining project review, one year after completion. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Infiltration in the lined reaches fell to near zero on post lining CCTV.
Manhole to manhole flow below the project rose at night after lining.
The liner sealed the mains but lateral connections were not sealed at the main.
Night CCTV at lateral junctions below the project shows clear water entering at unsealed connections.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A new subdivision added the extra night flow
The downstream meter was replaced and reads high
The liner is leaking along its whole length
Groundwater blocked from the mains now enters at unsealed lateral connections, moving the entry point

inference.explanation: Lined reaches test near zero, so a whole length liner leak is contradicted, and clear water is seen entering at the unsealed junctions. No new subdivision is stated, and the entry is visible, not a meter artifact.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Re-lining the same mains
Lateral connection sealing scoping for the project area, with night junction CCTV as the measure
A subdivision connection audit

clueText.nc-a: The mains already test near zero, so re-lining repeats sealed work.

clueText.nc-c: No new connections are recorded, and entry is visible at old junctions.

tasks.prompt: Spot repairs fix three collapsed points, yet backups continue on the same street at a new location each time.

Backup locations migrate along the street as each weakest point is repaired.

Each spot repair was installed incorrectly
Backups are caused by resident behaviour on this street
Roots alone explain all the street failures

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Continuing spot repairs one failure at a time
A resident behaviour campaign as the sole action
A full street rehabilitation options analysis, lining versus replacement, using the full CCTV condition grade

clueText.nc-c: The analysis shows full rehabilitation costs less than five more years of spot repairs and backups.

tasks.prompt: A supervisor must verify a CCTV contractor claim that 90 percent of a basin is in good condition.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario CCTV program audit with a resurvey sample. Observations are as stated.

The city resurvey crews are too strict and the contractor is right
The contractor grading is unreliable, and the 90 percent good claim should not be used for planning
Blocked reaches prove the city caused the defects after survey

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Retraining city resurvey crews to match the contractor
A full resurvey specification with coded defect verification and a quality holdback for the next contract
Accepting the summary for capital planning

clueText.nc-b: The new specification requires sample verification before payment on every survey batch.
clueText.nc-c: City coding matched the defects that later blocked, so the city standard is the reliable one.

tasks.prompt: Cleaning records claim a reach was jetted, but a backup there a week later shows the reach untouched.

The jetting truck GPS shows it never entered the street that day.
The same crew has three other signed orders on streets its GPS never visited.

Jetting marks fade within a week so the CCTV proves nothing
Residents reblocked the reach within a week of a proper jetting
The cleaning was not performed, and the signed records for that crew are not trustworthy

inference.explanation: Undisturbed deposits with no marks, a GPS track off the street, and a pattern across four orders outweigh a signature. A one week reblock to undisturbed condition and a month long GPS fault are not supported by any check.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A verification protocol, GPS matched to work orders plus random post cleaning CCTV, for all cleaning crews
Replacing the truck GPS as the sole action
Accepting the signed order and closing the audit

nextClue.explanation: Matching GPS to orders with random camera checks verifies work before backups test it.

clueText.nc-a: Under the protocol, the next quarter shows orders and GPS agreeing, with camera checks confirming cleaning.
clueText.nc-b: Closing the audit would leave a pattern of four false orders unaddressed.
clueText.nc-c: GPS agreed with other trucks and with fuel records, so the unit was working.

tasks.prompt: An operator in charge review finds a station alarm was acknowledged but no one attended for six hours.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario alarm response review under overall responsible operator duties in Regulation 129/04. Observations are as stated.

The response failed because the pump was left off after maintenance and the acknowledged alarm was not acted on
The alarm system sent a false alarm and no response was needed
Rain inflow made any response pointless

inference.explanation: Levels recovered when the pump was started manually, so it had not failed electrically, and a false alarm would not need a manual start to recover. The off mode after maintenance plus six hours without action is the verified chain.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Alarm system replacement
A post maintenance return to service checklist with alarm response attendance requirements
A rainfall review for that night

nextClue.explanation: A return to service checklist catches an off mode pump before an alarm tests it.

clueText.nc-a: The alarm was real, levels were high, so the system reported correctly.
clueText.nc-b: Checklist use after the next maintenance confirms both pumps in auto with alarms tested.
clueText.nc-c: No rain event is recorded that night, and inflow was normal.

tasks.prompt: A Class 3 operator compares cleaning methods after a basin cleaned by jetting alone reblocks in months, while a neighbouring basin cleaned with jetting plus CCTV stays clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario cleaning program comparison over two years. Observations are as stated.

Basin N, jetted with CCTV verification, has defects repaired as found and stays clear for two years.
Both basins have similar pipe age, trees, and food premises counts.

Basin N stays clear only because it is newer
Basin M residents misuse their sewers more than Basin N residents
Jetting without inspection treats symptoms while hidden defects in Basin M keep causing reblocks

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Jetting Basin M more often on the same fixed route
A resident misuse campaign as the sole action in Basin M
Adding CCTV verification and a defect repair list to the Basin M cleaning program

nextClue.explanation: Camera verification converts Basin M cleaning from symptom relief to defect finding, as in Basin N.

clueText.nc-a: More frequent jetting of the same reaches already failed for two years.
clueText.nc-b: No misuse difference is observed between the similar basins.
clueText.nc-c: In the first verified year, Basin M defects are listed and repaired, and reblocks fall sharply.

tasks.prompt: Force main pressure rises slowly for months, then a break occurs at a low point with heavy wall loss.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main failure review. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Pressure at the station rose 15 percent over eight months at the same flows.
The break is at a low point where an air valve was never installed and sediment collects.
Wall samples at the break show deep internal corrosion under a sediment layer.
A sister force main with air valves and a flushing program shows no similar wall loss at its low points.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: External soil corrosion caused the break
The pipe was defective from installation
Sediment and trapped gas at the unvented low point drove internal corrosion until the wall failed
The pressure rise alone burst a sound pipe

inference.explanation: Wall loss is internal under sediment, the sister main with venting and flushing is sound, and a 15 percent rise is far below what bursts sound pipe. The unvented low point is the difference that matches the damage location.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A soil corrosivity survey as the sole action
Replacing the broken section with no program review
Low point inspection and air valve and flushing provisions review for all force mains in the system

nextClue.explanation: Reviewing every main for unvented low points finds the same risk before another break.

clueText.nc-a: Section replacement alone leaves the corrosion mechanism in place.
clueText.nc-b: Damage is internal under sediment, not a soil side pattern.
clueText.nc-c: The review finds two more unvented low points with early wall loss, now scheduled for valves and flushing.

tasks.prompt: A surcharge in a trunk sewer during storms is traced by level loggers placed at five manholes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario trunk surcharge investigation with level logging. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Loggers show surcharge starting at the lowest manhole and backing up from there.
The lowest reach contains a partially collapsed section found on CCTV, reducing its bore.
Reaches above the collapse show no defects and normal levels in dry weather.
Removing storm inflow in a model still leaves the collapsed reach as the first point of surcharge.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The partially collapsed low reach is the bottleneck that starts the surcharge
A downstream treatment plant restriction backs up the trunk
The loggers were installed in the wrong order
Total storm inflow exceeds trunk design everywhere equally

inference.explanation: Surcharge beginning at the defective reach, a measured bore reduction, and modelling that keeps the collapse as the start point all agree. A plant restriction would raise the downstream end first beyond the collapse, and logger order was verified by the dry weather baseline.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A system wide inflow reduction program as the first step
A plant restriction review as the sole action
Collapse repair scoping with pre and post repair level logging in a matched storm

nextClue.explanation: Logging the repair in a matched storm verifies the bottleneck is gone.

clueText.nc-a: Inflow reduction may help later, but the collapse is the measured start point.
clueText.nc-b: Plant levels during events were normal in the same records.
clueText.nc-c: After repair, the matched storm passes with levels below surcharge at all five manholes.

tasks.prompt: A wet weather bypass at a lift station is reviewed: the station ran all pumps, yet inflow still exceeded discharge for two hours.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wet weather bypass review, Class 3 level. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: All pumps ran through the event and delivered their combined tested capacity.
Catchment inflow peaked at 140 percent of station discharge capacity for two hours.
Rainfall was a one in two year event, well within the range the system should handle by reducing inflow sources.
Basin flow data show one sub-basin contributing half the peak from direct inflow sources.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pumps underperformed during the storm
Excess direct inflow from one sub-basin, not station performance, caused the bypass
Operators started the pumps too late
The rain was an extreme beyond any reasonable design

inference.explanation: Pumps delivered tested capacity from the start, the rain was a routine one in two year event, and half the peak is traced to one sub-basin of direct sources. Station performance is measured as full, so inflow is the gap.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A pump capacity upgrade as the first project
Operator retraining on pump start timing
Direct inflow source removal in the contributing sub-basin, with storm flow verification

nextClue.explanation: Removing the traced inflow sources attacks the measured half of the peak.

clueText.nc-a: Pumps already deliver full tested capacity, so upgrades chase the wrong side.
clueText.nc-b: Start logs show pumps running before the peak arrived.
clueText.nc-c: After source removal, a matched storm peak falls below station capacity with no bypass.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints return each summer at a subdivision edge where a long gravity sewer runs slow and shallow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario summer odour investigation at a subdivision edge. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Complaints occur only in hot months and only in the evening.
The sewer is long, flat, and runs shallow in the evening low flow period.
Sulfide measured in the evening is high, and morning readings after higher flows are low.
A parallel subdivision with a steeper, shorter sewer to the same trunk has no complaints.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Evening cooking odours from homes are mistaken for sewer odour
A landfill near the subdivision causes the summer odours
The trunk sewer backs gas up only this branch in summer
Long slow evening flow in hot weather lets sewage turn septic and release sulfide at the edge manholes

inference.explanation: Sulfide itself is measured high in the evening and low after flushing flows, which cooking and landfill claims do not explain. The steeper parallel branch with the same trunk connection has no problem, separating branch conditions from trunk gas.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: Evening sulfide logging across a hot week, paired with a flushing trial on the flat reach
A home cooking survey
A landfill odour study

nextClue.explanation: A flushing trial tests whether moving the slow evening flow removes the sulfide peak.

clueText.nc-a: Flushing on trial evenings cuts measured sulfide and complaints stop on those evenings.
clueText.nc-b: Sulfide is measured inside the sewer, so a landfill study does not address it.
clueText.nc-c: Cooking odours do not raise sewer sulfide readings.

tasks.prompt: A manhole in a busy road shows rapid bench and wall deterioration two years after a force main was rerouted into it.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole deterioration investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Before rerouting, the manhole served gravity flow only and showed no deterioration in 20 years.
The rerouted force main carries septic sewage with long detention from a distant station.
Deterioration is worst on the wall facing the force main discharge and fades around the bench.
A second manhole receiving the same force main flow after a drop shows the same pattern.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The manhole concrete was always weak and failed by age
Road salt and traffic loading suddenly damaged the manhole
Septic force main discharge turbulence releases sulfide that attacks the manhole at the discharge point
Gravity sewage became stronger after rerouting

inference.explanation: Twenty sound years rule out weak concrete by age, damage centred on the discharge face fits turbulent release, and the second discharge manhole repeats the pattern. Traffic and salt do not centre damage on a discharge face inside the structure.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

options.label: A road salt study for the corridor
Rebuilding the manhole in plain concrete with no protection
Discharge manhole protection scoping, lining or coating, at both force main discharge manholes

nextClue.explanation: Protecting both discharge manholes addresses the repeated pattern inspection found.

clueText.nc-a: Salt does not explain damage centred inside on the discharge face.
clueText.nc-b: Plain rebuilding repeats the 20 year sound history only until septic discharge resumes attack.

tasks.prompt: A FOG blockage forms below a hospital kitchen despite a large, well maintained interceptor.

evidence.label: The interceptor is large, serviced on schedule, and its outlet sample is low in grease.

The pantry disposes of cooking oil from a small fryer into its sink daily.
Above the pantry junction the sewer is clean, below it grease builds.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

The interceptor is failing despite its clean outlet sample
A small unprotected pantry drain, not the main kitchen, is the grease source
The sewer below the hospital is too flat and collects any grease

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

A hospital wide grease education campaign as the sole action
Upsizing the main interceptor further

nextClue.explanation: Routing the pantry through treatment closes the exact gap the junction pattern found.

clueText.nc-b: The main interceptor outlet already tests low, so size is not the gap.

tasks.prompt: A supervisor reviews why one district has triple the blockage rate of a similar district after both adopted the same cleaning schedule.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario two district blockage comparison, same cleaning schedule. Observations are as stated.

The schedule works in Q so P records must be exaggerated
District P crews clean less carefully than District Q crews
District P pipes are secretly older than records show

Equal extra cleaning in both districts
A FOG enforcement focus in District P, with blockage type tracked monthly

tasks.prompt: A new Class 3 operator inherits a basin where infiltration was claimed fixed, but spring flows say otherwise, and must plan the audit.

Post project monitoring in the files covers only one dry summer month.
No control basin was monitored during the project.

The project failed because its contractor was changed midway
The success claim is unproven because monitoring covered only a dry month with no control, and current spring flows match baseline
Infiltration returned because residents added connections this year

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation?

A spring season night flow audit with a matched control basin before any new capital is approved
A meter replacement as the sole audit step
